title: Frederick II (ministerial rescript) to Louis Michell (London), Berlin 28 Dec 1751, KHA Prins Willem V inv. 198 (DECODE R1955), in Michell's envoy code

steps.what: Fetched DECODE R1955 (and R1957, targets/michell1751/) images with the cookie.
R1955 (the other letter of the same date, ministerial rescript) transcribed in full: 362 groups.
R1955 vs R1957: 19 shared distinct groups, chance collisions; 296 distinct in 362, commonest group 5 times: large homophonic code with nothing for ciphertext-only analysis.
Printed or online decipherment of R1955 sought; the ministerial rescripts are not in the Politische Correspondenz; none found.
DECODE R1953 (von der Hellen to the King, 4 Jan 1752) checked as a sibling of R1955: different, smaller code.
WAINUT: R1955 transcribed independently from the DECODE images (360 groups; one unsplit nine-digit run) (R1955_tx.txt).
WAINUT: R1955 against the cabinet keys: v1 gives a value to 10 of 360 groups (2.8%), v2 to 20 (5.6%), against 181 of 548 (33.0%) and 381 (69.5%) for R1957: R1955 is not in the cabinet code.

WAINUT: table of Michell's envoy code (271 codes, 512 pairs) built from DECODE's transcriptions of the contemporary Dutch decipherments of Michell's reports R1050 and R1051 (key1751/scripts/envoy_key.py; table not committed); applied to R1955: 95 of 360 groups (26.4%) decoded; adjacent decoded words attested as French word pairs 19 of 30 against 11.1 for permutations (p = 0.001; with PC 8-9 only as corpus 14 vs 9.5, p = 0.046; the right v1 decode of R1957 scores only p = 0.28 on this test).

WAINUT circular-letter test, rule fixed in advance: LCS of R1955's 77 decoded words with each French PC 8-9 letter, z against 100 shuffles; best candidate (22 Dec 1751 - 10 Jan 1752) PC 5268 z = 2.69, highest control PC 5117 z = 4.85; no candidate qualifies; positive control finds a 17% word sample in its source at z 27.6-31.3 and in a 50% paraphrase at 5.8-10.9 (key1751/scripts/circular.py).

WAINUT prior-art check: this folder's predecessor (michell1751, Bourdeau, 19 Sep 2026) had transcribed R1955. A contemporary Dutch decipherment of R1955 may exist in Nationaal Archief 1.01.50 inv. 159 (not digitised); not consulted.
WAINUT transcriptions compared with Bourdeau's (compare_tx.py): R1955 352 of 360 groups agree, 8 differences.

Split from michell1751 under the one-key rule (Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): R1955 is in Michell's envoy code, not the cabinet code of R1957, so it is its own entry. Fraction re-counted from R1955_reading_line.txt: 95 of 360 groups have a value.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): both transcriptions (Bourdeau transcription_r1955.txt, WAINUT R1955_tx.txt) and WAINUT's group-by-group decode R1955_reading_line.txt (95/360 groups)

Reading audit (George Lasry's test: can a reader build coherent sentences and translate them?). R1955_reading_line.txt read: a single line of 1,660 characters, about three quarters '·', with single words and short fragments between unread groups; no sentence can be built (docs/_check_reading.py finds no scoreable sentence). Relabelled decoded, not read; class read in part -> not read, method read after matching with key from external sources -> not solved (the match kept as a part); fraction_read 0.264 -> 0.

Re-read (REREAD_BRIEF, batch b32): DECODE R1955 fetched logged in (b28_fetch.py); both full-resolution pages opened: cipher, clear heading/opening/date only, no decipherment, no attachment or comment. Cached DECODE list searched for other records in the envoy code: only R1050/R1051. Envoy table covers 8-12% of the von der Hellen letters (chance level): not his code.

Nationaal Archief 1.10.29 (Fagel) inv. 5177 (187 scans) and inv. 5208 (157 scans) checked heading by heading through the archive's IIIF (b32_na_iiif.py, b32_sheet.py). 5208 holds 'Lettres Ecrites au Sieur M. en Novemb. et Decemb. 1751' nos. 1-8 (2 Nov - 7 Dec 1751), the Dutch clear decipherments of the ministerial rescripts in this code, and Michell's reports 1751-53 in clear; the 28 Dec 1751 rescript (R1955) is in neither volume, and the copies carry no figures, so no new code values.

Method restored: key obtained by matching the envoy-code table rebuilt from the decipherments of Michell's reports R1050/R1051 (read after matching with key from external sources); text not read, class stays not read. The 22-24 Oct reading audit had set the method to not solved because the class was not read; George Lasry (24 Oct 2026) separates the two.

validation.notes: Whole-word code decoded in isolated fragments (95 of 360 groups, mostly single words between unread groups); the letter n-gram test has no continuous text to score. WAINUT's word-pair coherence test (19 of 30 adjacent pairs attested against 11.1 for permutations, p = 0.001) is the statistical check.

outcome.method: read after matching with key from external sources
outcome.method_basis: The envoy-code table from the contemporary decipherments of Michell's reports R1050/R1051 matches R1955 (WAINUT; read after matching with key from external sources, recorded under parts), but gives a value to only 95 of 360 groups: fragments, no sentences. Method restored 24 Oct 2026 (George Lasry: a key can be mostly recovered while the text is not read): the key was obtained by matching the envoy-code table rebuilt from the decipherments of Michell's reports R1050/R1051; class stays not read, as the text does not read.
outcome.fraction_read_source: 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: the one document does not build sentences, so nothing counts as read (0). Withdrawn as a reading figure: 0.264, R1955_reading_line.txt (95 of 360 groups with a value from the envoy table), which counts valued groups, not sentences.

gaps.item: R1955, 265 of 360 groups without a value in the envoy table
gaps.detail: The table comes from two decipherments of Michell's reports (R1050, R1051); further decipherments (probably KHA A31-1181) are not online, and a contemporary decipherment of R1955 may be in Nationaal Archief 1.01.50 inv. 159, not digitised. Not in print: ministerial rescripts are not in the Politische Correspondenz.

outcome.notes: WAINUT's result (PR #29), checked here: transcription compared and fraction re-counted. The subject cannot be stated beyond Dutch affairs (the Prince Stadholder, the States) and a negotiation involving Vienna. Split 14 Oct 2026 from michell1751.

texts.label: Frederick II (ministerial rescript) to Louis Michell, Berlin, 28 Dec 1751 (DECODE R1955)
texts.summary: The ministerial rescript in the King's name to his envoy in London, opening in clear 'Toutes vos dépêches m'ont été bien rendues et la dernière est du 14e de ce mois', then 362 code groups. WAINUT decoded 95 of 360 groups (26.4%) with the envoy table rebuilt from the Dutch decipherments of Michell's reports R1050/R1051: fragments only, the subject cannot be stated with confidence.
texts.note: Decoded, not read: WAINUT's envoy-table decode gives values to 95 of 360 groups (single words and fragments, no sentence). Re-read 23 Oct 2026 (batch b32, R1955_reread_log.md): the DECODE record has only the two cipher pages (no decipherment, attachment or comment); no other DECODE record is in this code besides R1050/R1051; the Fagel decipherment registers 5177 (1751-52) and 5208 ('Sieur M', 1751-53) hold the Dutch clear copies of the rescripts to Michell nos. 1-8 (2 Nov - 7 Dec 1751) and of his reports, but not the rescript of 28 Dec 1751, and no figures. Blocker: no-key-material.

parts.label: R1955 (Michell's envoy code matched; decoded, not read)

parts.basis: WAINUT's table from the R1050/R1051 decipherments, 95 of 360 groups valued, adjacent words coherent above chance (19/30 against 11.1); fragments only. Decoded, not read (reading audit, 22 Oct 2026).

prior.where: Ministerial rescript, not in the Politische Correspondenz; no printed or online decipherment found

human: Supplied the DECODE login (session cookie) for the images.
